resolved_or_reduced: OS Open UPRN contains the UPRN and the point position of each AddressBase Premium record rather than a building or parcel polygon
OS Open UPRN GeoPackage geometry is a point in British National Grid derived from X and Y attributes and latitude longitude are ETRS89 coordinates
OS Open UPRN FID is non-persistent and cannot be used as a durable join key
OS Open Linked Identifiers is supplied as 11 relationship packages with CSV relationship data and JSON product version information
Relationship 5 links BLPU UPRN to TopographicArea TOID and includes live provisional and historic BLPU records
Relationship 5 is formed by Address seed point-in-polygon correlation and is not evidence of ownership or legal parcel extent
AddressBase Premium and OS MasterMap Topography Layer have different release cycles so a published relationship can be out of sync
Linked Identifier confidence states distinguish correct potentially changed and changed version information
OS states that the latest identifier version metadata can differ from the feature version originally used to form the relationship and the relationship may no longer be valid
OS Open USRN supplies one simplified line geometry per USRN and the line represents street extent rather than a road or property boundary
Ofcom Spring 2026 full-fibre availability and gigabit coverage headline figures use residential premises while full-fibre take-up and decent-broadband-unavailable figures use all premises
Ofcom local-authority full-fibre take-up has separate denominators for premises with full-fibre coverage and for all premises
A decrease in full-fibre take-up percentage of covered premises can occur while active connections increase because the coverage denominator grows faster
Ofcom planned deployment results use the same fixed January 2026 premise base and must remain separate from the current-coverage snapshot
Planned network counts include overbuild and multiple gigabit-capable networks at the same residential premise
BDUK monthly contract progress tables contain initial-scope contracted premises and may exclude deferred-scope premises
BDUK monthly contract tables are rounded to the nearest ten and can contain ingestion lag between delivery and the published snapshot
Supplier resubmissions can reduce previously reported built-premises counts without indicating a deterioration in delivery performance
BDUK monthly contractual management information is not directly comparable with official subsidy-delivery statistics
BDUK official delivery statistics remove overbuild and may be reported up to six months after a premises was built
BDUK states that its premises base cannot be precisely compared with Ofcom's premises base
HMLR Title Descriptor tenure does not change while a non-absolute class of title can be upgraded after an evidenced application
Title Descriptor can change more than once within a month but the monthly publication contains only the latest state
